Narendra Chandra Das and another ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Sree Sree Gopal Bigraha and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 5. The present defendant petitioners contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made by the plaintiffs. Their material case was that the suit property was recorded in the name of deity Sree Sree Gopal Jew Bigraha as a rent receiver and one Hari Priya Biasnabi as its shebait. That Hari Priya Biasnabi used to reside in the suit land and when she grew old and unable to move she brought Khepa Chand Bairagi to reside in the suit property. That in 1948 Hari Priya Biasnabi died and after her death her only heir Khepa Chand Bairagi inherited the suit property and possessed the same. That there was no deity in the suit property and the C.S. recorded bargader also did not possess the same. That after wholesale acquisition the suit property vested in the Government and thereafter in 1951 Khepa Chand Bairagi took pattan of the suit land in his name from government and possessed the same as his own property. That he never performed any religious rites of the deity. That on 31.01.1977 Khepa Chand Bairagi transferred the suit property by a deed of gift in favour of his two sons and wife-the defendants. That these defendants mutated their names vide Mutation Case No. 1052/84-85 and paid rent to the Government. That on 03.01.1990 the defendants came to know that the mutation case had been cancelled and the khatian has been restored. The defendants thereafter filed an objection case which was allowed and the suit land stood recorded in the name of the defendants. That the plaintiffs in collusion with some local notorious persons forcibly dispossessed the defendants from 5x6 yards of land of the suit property and installed a deity there, but in fact there was never any deity in the suit property before.
